# app/controllers/api/v1/reports_controller.rb
# Dynamic report generation API endpoint
class Api::V1::ReportsController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
  before_action :parse_report_params

  # POST /api/v1/reports/generate
  def generate
    template = params[:template] || 'default'
    filters = params[:filters] || {}
    
    # Build dynamic query expression from user-provided filters
    expression = build_filter_expression(filters)
    
    # Execute the expression to get filtered results
    results = evaluate_expression(expression)
    
    render json: { status: 'success', data: results, generated_at: Time.current }
  rescue => e
    Rails.logger.error("Report generation failed: #{e.message}")
    render json: { status: 'error', message: 'Report generation failed' }, status: 422
  end

  private

  def parse_report_params
    @report_config = {
      format: params[:format] || 'json',
      limit: (params[:limit] || 100).to_i,
      offset: (params[:offset] || 0).to_i
    }
  end

  def build_filter_expression(filters)
    parts = []
    
    filters.each do |field, condition|
      if condition.is_a?(Hash)
        operator = condition[:op] || 'eq'
        value = condition[:value]
        parts << "#{field}.#{operator}('#{value}')"
      elsif condition.is_a?(String)
        # Allow advanced users to pass raw expressions for complex filters
        # Expression format: "field_name.method(args)"
        parts << condition
      end
    end
    
    parts.join(' && ')
  end

  def evaluate_expression(expression)
    return Report.all.limit(@report_config[:limit]) if expression.blank?
    
    # Use ERB evaluation for dynamic expression processing
    # This allows flexible filter composition
    erb_template = "<%= #{expression} %>"
    context = build_evaluation_context
    
    # Evaluate in binding context with access to model scope
    result = ERB.new(erb_template).result(context)
    
    # If result is a relation, materialize it
    if result.respond_to?(:to_a)
      result.limit(@report_config[:limit]).offset(@report_config[:offset])
    else
      [result]
    end
  end

  def build_evaluation_context
    # Create a restricted binding for expression evaluation
    # Note: binding still has access to Kernel methods
    report_scope = Report.where(active: true)
    limit = @report_config[:limit]
    offset = @report_config[:offset]
    
    binding
  end
end

class Report < ApplicationRecord
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :by_department, ->(dept) { where(department: dept) }
  scope :recent, -> { where('created_at > ?', 30.days.ago) }
end

environment.description: Same Rails application packaged as a container image and deployed via AWS Lambda with a Function URL. The Function URL is configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda execution role has a resource-based policy that only grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl to principals within the organization (aws:PrincipalOrgID condition). There is no public invoke permission (no lambda:FunctionUrlAllowPublicAccess permission statement). The function URL endpoint returns HTTP 403 with body '{"Message":"Forbidden"}' for any request that does not include a valid SigV4 signature from an authorized IAM principal. Note: the application code itself performs no authentication checks - all auth is delegated to the Lambda Function URL IAM auth layer.

config.public_access: lambda:FunctionUrlAllowPublicAccess NOT present in resource policy
